chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Nafi' al-Bajali, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Do not associate anything with Allah, and even if you are burnt in the fire and punished, your heart should remain at rest with faith; and your parents, so obey them and be righteous to them, whether they are alive or dead; and if they order you to leave your family and your wealth, do so, for that is from faith."'
ai.seo_question: What are the essential elements of faith and parental duty according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the endurance of severe trials to the purity of monotheism (tawhid), illustrating that true faith provides inner tranquility even amidst physical suffering. The hadith further elevates parental righteousness (birr al-walidayn) to a pillar of faith, extending obedience beyond their lifetime and even to the point of leaving one's home and wealth if commanded, a point of emphasis in Shia jurisprudence regarding the scope of filial duty.
